proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: induction on n reduces to the case where all g_i lie on one connected component (a clopen decomposition splits the problem into two disjoint affine opens whose disjoint union is affine); translating by g_1^{-1} puts the points in G^0 (0B7R); irreducibility of G^0 makes the finite intersection of translates U g_i^{-1} nonempty, and local finite type over the algebraically closed field gives a rational point g in the intersection, so all g_i lie in the affine open g^{-1}U (source lines 1553-1579)

core_obligations: Component reduction (proof lines 1554-1561): a clopen decomposition separating the points splits into smaller instances; the two affine opens meet the clopen pieces in disjoint affine opens, and their union (a disjoint union of affines) is affine, so by induction all g_i share a component; translating by g_1^{-1} places them in G^0 (0B7R).

Translate intersection (proof lines 1562-1579): for affine U containing e, each U g_i^{-1} is a nonempty open of the irreducible G^0, so the finite intersection is nonempty; G^0 locally of finite type over the algebraically closed k has a k-rational point g in the intersection; then g_i in g^{-1}U for all i and g^{-1}U is affine.
proof_roadmap: Induct to place all points on one component (proof lines 1554-1561).
Intersect the translates inside the irreducible G^0 and pick a rational point g (proof lines 1562-1579).
